transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Oct 3 2028 14:30 UTC
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Evan, Priya (Redwood); David, Maya, Ollie (Northlight)

Summary (auto): quick security onramp to understand compliance gating for inference at telco edge.

[00:00:05] Evan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, i'm Evan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] David: good thanks, uh excited to get into this — we have a bunch of questions specifically around how you handle encryption across regions and also how we can integrate SSO.
[00:00:20] Priya: great, can i kick off with a quick agenda? i'll run through certs and auth, then we can go into logging and retention and finally kvm — sorry k-m-s stuff and bring-your-own-key details.
[00:00:28] Maya: perfect, yes pls start with certs.
[00:00:31] Priya: okay — SOC2 and ISO, short answer is we are SOC 2 Type II and we also hold ISO 27001, we can share redacted reports and the auditor contact, typical artifacts. for hosted customers the control plane and runtime are covered, for Dedicated there's contract language for separation and for Private we provide the on-prem package and guidance for customer-run attestations.
[00:00:52] Ollie: when you say covered, do you mean Redwood manages the keys in hosted or can we bring our own keys to the runtime?
[00:00:59] Priya: hosted by default uses Redwood-managed encryption at rest and in transit; however we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private via KMS integrations — you can bring a cloud KMS in a VPC or an external HSM in Private deployments. note some hardware-backed HSMs need additional network setup for edge zones.
[00:01:18] David: edge zones is our main ask — we run telco edge nodes in multiple countries and we need encryption keys to be physically in those jurisdictions for some payloads. can you support regional KMS scoping?
[00:01:28] Priya: yes, for Private deployments you control KMS and can localize keys. for Dedicated we can configure key routing to customer-managed KMS per-region if it's in the same cloud provider and network peering is established. hosted cannot hold customer keys in arbitrary regions due to multi-tenant constraints — we can discuss a dedicated-hosted hybrid where sensitive workloads route to Dedicated pools.
[00:01:49] Maya: that hybrid model might work. now on authentication — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[00:01:55] Evan: yes, SAML SSO with SSO providers like Okta, Azure AD, and supporting SCIM user sync is standard. Priya will go over role mapping.
[00:02:04] Priya: role mapping — we expose RBAC with roles at org, project, and route level. you can map your SAML groups to Redwood roles. common pattern we've seen at telcos is to create a tenants group mapped to an "inference-admin" role and separate groups for auditors and devops with read-only tokens. we also support short-lived tokens for CLI and service accounts.
[00:02:27] David: do tokens include scoping to model/version? like can we limit a service account to only call a specific model or route?
[00:02:33] Priya: yes, policy-based scoping is supported — you can restrict by model name, route, or environment. we call them routing policies; they can also force fallback behavior so if a model is unavailable calls can go to a cheaper or local variant.
[00:02:46] Ollie: sounds good. on audit logs — what granularity do you capture and how long are logs retained? also export options?
[00:02:54] Priya: audit logs capture API calls, user actions in console, policy changes, and deployment events. retention defaults to 90 days on hosted, with add-on retention up to several years. logs are exportable in JSONL to S3 (for Hosted we export to an s3 we control; for Dedicated/Private we can ship logs to your S3 or SIEM over TLS). we also support syslog/structured streaming to Splunk or Datadog.
[00:03:18] Maya: for compliance we need write-once logs and tamper evidence, is that available?
[00:03:23] Priya: for Dedicated and Private, you can configure immutable retention in your storage layer (S3 Object Lock) and we recommend routing audit logs there. for hosted customers we maintain internal immutability controls and can provide attestations but not customer-configurable object locking today.
[00:03:40] David: retention policy question — our call detail records (CDRs) are sensitive and the retention rules differ by country and by customer contract; we might need per-tenant retention windows and selective deletion. can Redwood support per-tenant retention?
[00:03:53] Priya: per-tenant retention on data we store is possible for Private; for Dedicated we can implement retention rules at the instance level and via routing policies to storage buckets with lifecycle rules. hosted is more rigid — retention is set at org level but we can work with legal on DPA clauses for specific customers.
[00:04:10] Ollie: legal audits will ask for data lineage and provenance, can you annotate inference requests with request IDs tied back to original CDRs?
[00:04:18] Priya: yes, you can pass metadata headers and we preserve that as part of the request record; audit exports include tags/metadata. also we have token-level cost traces that correlate to request IDs if needed for billing and traceability.
[00:04:30] Maya: one more on encryption — do you do envelope encryption and what KDFs/algorithms are used?
[00:04:36] Priya: we use envelope encryption; at rest we use AES-256-GCM. when integrating with KMS we do a key-wrapping model — KMS signs and unwraps per-region as needed. for edge setups we can support hardware-backed keys (PKCS11) and FIPS 140-2 modules in Private.
[00:04:54] David: regulatory wise we have lawful intercept obligations, and that means we might need the ability to export certain logs to regulators. how do you handle exports and chain of custody?
[00:05:03] Evan: operationally, we can support secure exports to your control plane or SFTP endpoint with signed manifests; for Dedicated/Private the customer owns the export workflow. we'll need to draft a process with your compliance team to satisfy chain of custody.
[00:05:17] [crosstalk]
[00:05:20] Maya: when you say chain of custody you'll provide signatures on the payload?
[00:05:23] Evan: yes, we can sign export manifests and include checksums.
[00:05:26] Priya: quick note on performance trade-offs — encryption at rest and customer-managed KMS adds a small latency bump per cold start and key unwrap; for streaming and short-latency workloads at the edge we recommend Dedicated or Private pinned pools to avoid PKI round trips.
[00:05:43] David: understood, latency is critical for call routing and real-time features. what's your SLA for p99 latency on a dedicated pool?
[00:05:50] Priya: Dedicated p99 depends on instance type but we publish performance profiles — typical p99 is sub-200ms for small-medium models with continuous batching disabled; for streaming workloads we can tune concurrency and batching to hit p99 targets, and we have canary deploys and automatic fallback policies if a pool degrades.
[00:06:07] Ollie: curious: do you have customer references in telecom?
[00:06:11] Evan: we do, a few telco platform teams use our Dedicated mode and we've run pilots for edge inference; happy to introduce after we sign an NDA.
[00:06:18] Maya: ok let's talk compliance docs now — can you share your data processing addendum and SOC2 controls matrix?
[00:06:23] Evan: yes i'll send the DPA and controls matrix. Priya will include the mapping to ISO controls you asked earlier.
[00:06:29] [00:06:29] Priya: another operational question — how do you want to handle environment separation? do you want dev/stage/prod in same org or separated?
[00:06:36] David: prefer strict separation, prod in separate account with separate keys.
[00:06:39] Priya: that's standard — we recommend separate VPCs and separate KMS keys per environment, and short-lived service accounts to limit blast radius.
[00:06:46] Maya: about RBAC again — do you support audit-only roles that cannot change policies but can annotate incidents?
[00:06:52] Priya: yes, auditor roles are read-only plus comment annotations; we also support a separate compliance role with the ability to export logs but not modify runtime configs.
[00:07:02] David: what's your approach to pentest and vulnerability disclosure?
[00:07:05] Evan: we do annual third-party pentests and have a vulnerability disclosure policy and program — can share redacted reports and the process for coordinated disclosure.
[00:07:13] Ollie: one operational edge detail — many of our sites are off-net and have intermittent connectivity, so we need to be able to run inference in an air-gapped mode or with local caching for KV; how does Redwood approach KV cache and offline inference?
[00:07:26] Priya: Private deployments can be fully air-gapped and we support local KV caching; for Dedicated we offer prefix/KV caching strategies and routing to local pools. hosted is not suitable for air-gapped edge.
[00:07:38] Maya: okay that clarifies.
[00:07:41] [long silence 00:07:42-00:08:05 while screen share is set up]
[00:08:06] Priya: moving on — i'll outline a sample SAML mapping: group -> role mapping, recommended session timeouts (we suggest short sessions for admin), and token rotation cadence. also we'll send an example SAML metadata xml and a SCIM payload example.
[00:08:27] David: great, please include step-by-step for Okta.
[00:08:30] Priya: will do.
[00:08:32] Evan: for timeline, what are you aiming for? pilot by end of q4 or q1?
[00:08:37] Ollie: q4 pilot would be ideal but realistic is early q1. security approvals tend to take 6–8 weeks.
[00:08:45] Maya: plus we need to run a proof-of-concept at one edge cluster and do load and compliance tests.
[00:08:51] Priya: ok we can scope a 4–6 week POC — included: Dedicated pool or Private sandbox, SOC2 artifact review, SAML integration, audit log export to your S3, and basic retention rules for CDR samples.
[00:09:05] David: what's the kickoff action from your side?
[00:09:08] Evan: i'll share SOC2/ISO docs and DPA; Priya will draft RBAC and SAML checklist; then we'll sync again to scope POC and pricing.
[00:09:18] Maya: any licensing or procurement blockers we should know about?
[00:09:21] Evan: procurement will require the DPA and security questionnaire; for Dedicated/Private we also typically sign an enterprise addendum for support and uptime SLAs.
[00:09:30] David: sponsors on our side will be me and Ollie, security reviewer is Maya, we'll loop in procurement after you send docs.
[00:09:37] [00:09:38] Evan: tidy next steps: i'll email artifacts; Priya will prepare RBAC/SAML docs; David to share anonymized CDR. we'll schedule the technical deep dive week of Oct 16. does that sound right?
[00:09:52] Maya: yes.
[00:09:54] Ollie: yes.
[00:09:56] Evan: awesome thanks all, we'll follow up via email and i'll create a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[00:10:02] [meeting continues with some clarifying Qs and small interruptions, total duration 55m]
